tip: The -s ending can mark a passive or a deponent (active meaning). Here träffas is deponent: it means meet each other, not is met.
Lyckas ends in -s but is active, not passive: vi lyckas means we succeed, not we are succeeded. It only exists in this -s form.
Skulle ha stannat covers both a neutral would have stayed and a regretful should have stayed. Context tells you which one is meant.
Unlike English, Swedish past participles inflect like adjectives: en stängd dörr, ett stängt hus, and den stängda dörren.
The particle upp reshapes the verb: ringa alone means to call, but ringer upp means to phone someone back.
Under all kritik literally means below all criticism: something so bad it is beyond critiquing at all.
Ta skeden i vacker hand literally means take the spoon in a fair hand: grit your teeth and make the best of a hard situation.
Swedish can move the object to the front for contrast: Pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi means money we lack, but time we have.
Swedish can place the bare verb first for emphasis: Sjunga kan hon means sing, she really can.
Torde is a formal, mostly written modal for cautious probability: det torde vara möjligt means it should presumably be possible.
Swedish genitive is just -s with no apostrophe: sommarens dagar means summer's days. Do not add an apostrophe like in English.
Adding -s to the past tense (here -des) forms the passive: hördes means was heard.
